title: Etale locality of punctual cohomological purity
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

Let $f:Y\to X$ be an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] between regular Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible. For every $y\in Y$ and $x=f(y)$, $Y$ is punctually pure at $y$ if and only if $X$ is punctually pure at $x$. Consequently, $X$ is punctually pure if and only if every member $Y_\alpha$ of any jointly surjective family of etale morphisms $Y_\alpha\to X$ with regular Noetherian $Y_\alpha$ is punctually pure. Jointly surjective means that every point of $X$ belongs to the image of at least one $Y_\alpha$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2 and the strict-henselization invariance stated after Definition 3.2.1, printed p.244; applied to etale neighbourhoods in the concluding reduction from Proposition 3.6.5 to Theorem 3.6.2, printed p.253.

proof.text: Fix $y\mapsto x$, and put $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $S=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $k=\kappa(x)$ and $k'=\kappa(y)$. Choose affine neighbourhoods of $y$ and $x$ on which $f$ is given by an etale ring map, as allowed by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. By [lem-sc-etale-local-dimension] the dimensions of $R,S$ are the same integer $d$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable] $k'/k$ is finite separable. Both local schemes are regular Noetherian by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Their closed-point immersions are regular by [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus]; their codimension is $d$ because the maximal ideals of these regular local rings have $d$ generators. Write $\eta_R:A_k\to j_R^!A_R(d)[2d]$ and $\eta_S:A_{k'}\to j_S^!A_S(d)[2d]$ for the classes in the statement. Thus no dimension shift or Tate twist changes between the two purity tests.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2, p.244; strict-henselization invariance

proof.text: Take any geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ above $y$ and put $\bar x=f\bar y$. An etale algebra is an ind-etale algebra by the constant one-object filtered presentation. Hence [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance], applied to $f$, gives the canonical isomorphism $Y_{(\bar y)}\cong X_{(\bar x)}$ over $X$. By [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison], these are the spectra of the algebraic strict henselizations of $S$ and $R$ respectively, with their specified residue embeddings into $\Omega$. Denote the common strict local scheme by $C$. This use of the comparison includes its equality on residue-field evaluations; it does not identify the two ordinary local schemes or the two residue fields.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2, p.244; strict-henselization invariance

proof.text: The maps $\rho_R:C\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\rho_S:C\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ are affine and ind-etale by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-affine-chart-ind-etale], applied to each local scheme. The scheme $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian] and regular by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular]; its dimension is $d$ by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension]. Apply [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian] to $j_R$ and to $j_S$. Their base changes to $C$ are both the closed point $c\hookrightarrow C$: the strict localization of a residue-field spectrum at the chosen geometric point is its separable-closure spectrum. For a field the maximal ideal is zero, so [lem-sc-ring-strict-henselization-local-maximal-ideal] says its strict henselization has zero maximal ideal and is a field; [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] identifies its residue field with the chosen separable closure and identifies the geometric evaluation. In particular these are Cartesian squares of pairs, not squares obtained by replacing a whole etale fibre by one point.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2, p.244; strict-henselization invariance

proof.text:
Write $i:c\hookrightarrow C$, $a_R:c\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a_S:c\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ for the arrows of those squares. Apply [lem-per-ind-etale-closed-support-base-change] to each square, with finite coefficient ring $A=\mathbf F_\ell$ and complex $A_R(d)[2d]$ or $A_S(d)[2d]$. Its hypotheses hold by Step 3, with no excellence or constructibility requirement. Using [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] to identify the pulled-back constant Tate lines gives
$$a_R^*j_R^!A_R(d)[2d]\cong i^!A_C(d)[2d]\cong a_S^*j_S^!A_S(d)[2d].$$
Under these specific base-change comparisons, [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] identifies both $a_R^*\eta_R$ and $a_S^*\eta_S$ with $\eta_i:A_c\to i^!A_C(d)[2d]$. Its strict-localization compatibility preserves the Kummer normalization. Thus it is the maps themselves that agree, not just their source and target objects.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2, p.244; strict-henselization invariance

proof.text: Let $h:\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Take geometric fibres of the two equal maps in Step 4 at $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to c$. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] these fibres are the fibres of $\eta_R$ at $\bar x$ and $\eta_S$ at $\bar y$; the same stalk comparison identifies the first with the fibre of $h^*\eta_R$ at $\bar y$. Inverse image on constant-$A$ module sheaves is exact and agrees with abelian inverse image by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and stalks are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]. Thus these comparisons also identify every cohomology map of the fibres. Since $\bar y$ was arbitrary, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] shows that $\eta_S$ is an isomorphism if and only if $h^*\eta_R$ is. Apply that criterion to the underlying abelian complexes: a bijective $A$-linear cohomology map has $A$-linear inverse, so it detects the same isomorphisms in the coefficient category.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2, p.244; strict-henselization invariance

proof.text: The functor $h^*$ reflects isomorphisms here. Indeed, for any geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed] extends its embedding $k\to\Omega$ to $k'\to\Omega$, since $k'/k$ is finite separable by Step 1 and hence algebraic. This supplies a lift to $\operatorname{Spec}k'$. The stalk comparison [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] and exactness [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] identify all cohomology stalk maps downstairs with those upstairs at these lifts. The criterion [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] therefore reflects invertibility. Conversely any functor preserves an inverse. Combining this with Step 5 gives $\eta_S$ invertible if and only if $\eta_R$ invertible, proving the assertion at $y$ and $x$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definitions 3.2.1--3.2.2, p.244; strict-henselization invariance

proof.text: If $X$ is punctually pure, apply the pointwise equivalence just proved to every $y\in Y_\alpha$ for each $\alpha$, so that each $Y_\alpha$ is punctually pure. Conversely, suppose every $Y_\alpha$ is punctually pure. For any $x\in X$, joint surjectivity gives an $\alpha$ and a point $y\in Y_\alpha$ over $x$. The pointwise equivalence gives purity of $X$ at $x$. Quantifying over $x$ proves the converse. Empty schemes and an empty covering of the empty scheme are included: all relevant pointwise assertions are vacuous.

Step 2: f is ind-etale, so lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance plus the affine strict-local comparison give a common C = Spec R^sh = Spec S^sh. Step 3: C is Noetherian, regular, of dimension d, and ind-etale over both local schemes; 05WS Cartesian squares give the same closed point c, since the strict henselization of a field is its separable closure (via the local-max-ideal lemma). Step 4: ind-etale closed-support base change, Tate-line pullback and the class-calculus strict-localization compatibility identify a_R^*eta_R = eta_i = a_S^*eta_S as maps. Advisory: equating the item's adjoint j^! with the derived supported kernel on D^+ is elementary, by uniqueness of adjoints and t-exactness of i_*. Steps 5-6: geometric-stalk conservativity over all geometric points above y, plus lifting geometric points of Spec k to Spec k' (k'/k algebraic), give eta_S iso iff h^*eta_R iso iff eta_R iso. Step 7 is elementary. Edge cases checked: d=0, nontrivial residue extensions, f not surjective, no excellence, empty schemes. No duplicate: lem-per-punctual-strict-completion-test is the completion statement, not etale locality. Batch 5: the closure with and without the item proof is the same (16626 nodes, diff 0). lean.statement: theorem punctual_cohomological_purity_etale_locality (ℓ : ℕ) (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) : (∀ {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y], IsRegularScheme X → IsRegularScheme Y → ∀ (f : Y ⟶ X) [Etale f], IsUnit (ℓ : Γ(X, ⊤)) → IsUnit (ℓ : Γ(Y, ⊤)) → ∀ y : Y, IsPunctuallyPureAt ℓ hℓ Y y ↔ IsPunctuallyPureAt ℓ hℓ X (f y)) ∧ (∀ {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X], IsRegularScheme X → IsUnit (ℓ : Γ(X, ⊤)) → ∀ (I : Type v) (Y : I → Scheme.{u}) [∀ a : I, IsNoetherian (Y a)], (∀ a : I, IsRegularScheme (Y a)) → ∀ (f : ∀ a : I, Y a ⟶ X) [∀ a : I, Etale (f a)], (∀ x : X, ∃ (a : I) (y : Y a), f a y = x) → (IsPunctuallyPure ℓ hℓ X ↔ ∀ a : I, IsPunctuallyPure ℓ hℓ (Y a)))
